eli10.body:
A CMOS inverter is a light switch that uses zero power when it is ON or OFF.

Imagine two workers on a seesaw. Worker N sits on the ground side. Worker P sits on the power-supply side. When the input says HIGH, Worker N pulls the output to ground while Worker P lifts off. When the input says LOW, Worker P pulls the output to power while Worker N lifts off.

At any stable moment, exactly one worker is active and the other is resting. No current flows through the seesaw. Power is only spent during the brief instant when both workers are in motion — the switching transition.

This is why CMOS is king. 19 billion inverters on the A19 Pro, and they consume almost zero power when not switching. Without this property, your phone battery would last minutes, not hours.
eli10.pullquote: Two transistors, zero static power. That is the CMOS trick.

technical.body: A CMOS inverter pairs an NMOS (pull-down) with a PMOS (pull-up). Their gates are tied together (input), their drains are tied together (output). NMOS source connects to ground (VSS), PMOS source connects to supply (VDD). The key insight: when NMOS is ON, PMOS is OFF, and vice versa. There is never a DC path from VDD to ground in a stable state.

The VTC has five regions as Vin sweeps from 0 to VDD: Region 1 — PMOS ON/linear, NMOS OFF → Vout = VDD Region 2 — PMOS linear, NMOS saturation → Vout drops Region 3 — Both saturated → maximum gain, Vout transitions sharply Region 4 — PMOS saturation, NMOS linear → Vout approaches 0 Region 5 — PMOS OFF, NMOS ON/linear → Vout = 0

VM — switching threshold where Vin = Vout. For symmetric inverter: VM = VDD/2. NMH — noise margin HIGH = VOH − VIH. NML — noise margin LOW = VIL − VOL. VOH = VDD, VOL = 0 (ideal CMOS). For VM = VDD/2 (symmetric): (W/L)p / (W/L)n = μn/μp ≈ 2.5.

technical.h: GATE depth — what is actually tested
technical.body:
Switching threshold V<sub>M</sub> calculation (most common, 2-mark NAT). PMOS/NMOS sizing for symmetric switching. Noise margin computation. Power dissipation: P<sub>dynamic</sub> = C<sub>L</sub>V<sub>DD</sub>²f. Propagation delay t<sub>p</sub> and its dependence on transistor sizing.

VTC region identification and transistor state at a given V<sub>in</sub> appear as 1-mark MCQs.

realWorld.v: The A19 Pro is built from CMOS inverters — every NAND, NOR, flip-flop uses them
No DC path from V_DD to ground in stable states — key to battery life
P = C_L·V_DD²·f — at 4 GHz, this dominates total chip power
Reducing V_DD from 1.0V to 0.7V cuts dynamic power by half — the 3nm advantage
Full-swing output (0 to V_DD) gives maximum noise immunity — robust logic
PMOS is ~2.5× wider than NMOS to compensate for lower hole mobility
Sub-threshold leakage grows exponentially at small nodes — now 30–40% of total power

lab.title: A19 Pro · logic gate sizing
lab.brief: You are sizing the standard-cell library for the A19 Pro. Every logic gate starts from a CMOS inverter. For symmetric switching (V_M = V_DD/2), you need to calculate the PMOS width. Symmetric switching means equal noise margins — critical for robust logic at 3nm where noise is everywhere.
lab.hint: For V_M = V_DD/2 with equal thresholds, you need k_n = k_p, which means (W/L)_p = (μ_n/μ_p) × (W/L)_n.

solution.line: V<sub>M</sub> = V<sub>DD</sub>/2 requires k<sub>n</sub> = k<sub>p</sub> (when V<sub>tn</sub> = |V<sub>tp</sub>|)
PMOS must be 2.5× wider than NMOS because holes are 2.5× slower than electrons. This equalizes pull-up and pull-down strength.

pyqs.q: A CMOS inverter has V_DD = 1.8V, V_tn = 0.4V, |V_tp| = 0.4V, k_n = k_p. Find V_M in volts. (2 dp)
pyqs.trap: When k_n = k_p AND V_tn = |V_tp|, V_M = V_DD/2 = 0.9V. Students who use the general formula unnecessarily often make arithmetic errors.

sol.line: k<sub>n</sub> = k<sub>p</sub> and V<sub>tn</sub> = |V<sub>tp</sub>| → V<sub>M</sub> = V<sub>DD</sub>/2 = 0.90 V

pyqs.q: In a CMOS inverter at steady state (V_in = 0 or V_DD), the static power dissipation is:
pyqs.trap: At steady state, one transistor is OFF creating an open circuit. No DC path exists from V_DD to ground. Static power ≈ 0 (ignoring leakage). Dynamic power C_L·V_DD²·f only dissipates during switching.

sol.line: CMOS advantage: at V<sub>in</sub> = 0 or V<sub>DD</sub>, one transistor is OFF → no DC current → zero static power.

pyqs.q: A CMOS inverter switches at f = 1 GHz with C_L = 10 fF and V_DD = 1.0V. Find dynamic power in μW. (2 dp)
pyqs.trap: P = C_L·V_DD²·f = 10×10⁻¹⁵ × 1² × 10⁹ = 10×10⁻⁶ = 10 μW. Watch units carefully.

pyqs.q: To shift V_M of a CMOS inverter toward V_DD, you should:
pyqs.trap: Stronger NMOS (wider) increases k_n → r = √(k_n/k_p) increases → V_M moves up. Intuition: stronger pull-down means you need higher V_in to overcome it.

sol.line: V<sub>M</sub> = (V<sub>DD</sub> + V<sub>tp</sub> + V<sub>tn</sub>·r)/(1+r). Larger r (stronger NMOS) → V<sub>M</sub> shifts toward V<sub>DD</sub>.

pyqs.q: CMOS inverter: V_DD = 1.0V, V_tn = 0.3V, |V_tp| = 0.3V, k_n/k_p = 4. Find V_M in volts. (2 dp)
Reducing V_DD in a CMOS circuit from 1.0V to 0.7V reduces dynamic power by approximately:
pyqs.trap: P ∝ V_DD². Ratio = (0.7/1.0)² = 0.49. Reduction = 1 − 0.49 = 0.51 = 51%. V_DD scaling gives quadratic power savings.

pyqInsight.body: CMOS inverter is the highest-frequency topic in Electronic Devices alongside MOSFET I-V. V_M calculation, power dissipation, and noise margins appear almost every year.

practice.q: At the switching threshold V_M of a CMOS inverter, both transistors are in:
options: One is in linear, the other in cutoff
practice.why: At V_M, V_in = V_out. Both transistors satisfy V_DS > V_GS − V_t (for their respective thresholds), putting both in saturation. This is where the VTC slope is steepest — maximum voltage gain.

practice.q: V_DD = 3.3V, V_tn = |V_tp| = 0.7V, k_n = k_p. Find V_M in volts. (2 dp)
C_L = 50 fF, V_DD = 0.9V, f = 2 GHz. Find P_dynamic in μW. (2 dp)
The primary reason PMOS is made wider than NMOS in a CMOS inverter is:
options: PMOS needs more current to charge the output
Hole mobility is lower than electron mobility — wider compensates
practice.why: μ_p ≈ μ_n/2.5. To match the NMOS pull-down strength, the PMOS must be ~2.5× wider. This ensures symmetric switching (V_M = V_DD/2) and equal rise/fall times.

practice.q: V_OH = 1.0V, V_IH = 0.6V. Find NM_H in volts. (2 dp)
